newsitem.title: UK: Britain's MAM sells private Swiss bank to Safra.
newsitem.headline: Britain's MAM sells private Swiss bank to Safra.

text.p: British fund manager Mercury Asset Management (MAM) said on Monday it would sell its Swiss private bank Mercury Bank AG to Luxembourg-based Safra Republic Holdings SA for about 250 million Swiss francs ($192 million) cash.
In a joint statment, Safra said its flagship private bank, Republic National Bank of New York (Suisse) SA (RNB Suisse), would make the acquisition.
MAM said the deal was part of its stated strategy to concentrate on its core expertise of investment management, including its UK and Jersey based international private client business.

However, MAM said it was keeping its Swiss options for clients open in a separate deal with RNB under which it will introduce to the bank those of its clients "requiring the benefits of a Swiss banking service".
This arrangement complements another deal under which RNB Suisse has appointed MAM to manage "a significant pool of assets for its clients in equity and bond markets worldwide".
MAM said it would also maintain its representative office in Zurich through which it markets those of its mutual funds which are registered in Switzerland and other investment services.
A joint statement from the pair said the deal should close by the end of February 1997. ($1=1.3007 Swiss Franc)
